newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes Japan move on auto repair facilities.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes Japan move on auto repair facilities.

text.p: U.S. trade officials on Monday welcomed Japan's approval of two new types of car repair facilities, but said further measures were needed to open up Japan's automotive parts market.

"We are pleased that the Ministry of Transport has implemented this deregulatory action in accordance with the auto agreement," Commerce Secretary William Daley said in a statement. But he said the U.S. remains disappointed that Japan rejected a petition filed by the U.S. industry requesting that brake repairs be deregulated.

U.S. Trade Representative Designate Charlene Barshefsky said deregulation of car repair garages will open opportunities for more U.S. car part sales and benefit Japanese customers by helping to reduce prices.

"Make no mistake about it, unacceptable barriers remain in place," she added. "We will continue to work vigilantly to ensure that the government of Japan fully complies with the terms of the 1995 (car trade) agreement."
